items.why: Shape and color pairs map to meaning at a glance and suit recognition drills apart from text study.
Worded signs are read in context with the sign narrative and need no separate practice mode.

sections.heading: C — Traffic signs
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic signs

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A48
Road signs preach rules, hazards, position, routes and services, and their silhouettes and hues preview the message inside. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]
FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A48
Downward triangles order yielding at a sane pace with a halt if needed, while diamonds cry hazard ahead and beg caution with brakes at the ready. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]
FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A48
Eight-sided red always halts, demanding a full stop at the sign, line, crosswalk or curb, then deference to every crosser from both sides. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]
FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A48
Rectangles and squares carry orders, cautions and guidance, tall ones speaking law and wide ones pointing the way, while five-sided shields fence school ground and student crossings, their arrow plaques pinning the walk. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]
FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A48
Round signs foretell rails ahead and beg slower eyes and ears, and three-cornered pennants on the left rim of two-way two-lane roads open a marked no-passing stretch. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]
FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A49
Red signs always command obedience, from halts and yields to wrong-way bans, black and white ones either command or mark routes, yellow warns of road dangers and orange warns of work-zone dangers. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]
FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A49
Green guides to places, roads and distances, glowing yellow-green guards walkers, riders and pupils, blue guides to roadside services and brown to parks and playgrounds. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]
FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A49
Rule signs stand square, tall or special-cut in white, red or black, scripting direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and odd cases, with a red ring and slash branding the banned move. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]
FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A49
The eight-sided red stop board with pale letters freezes every wheel until crossers clear, and the red-and-white downward triangle throttles speed and surrenders passage to the busier road. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]
FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A49
A white bar floating in a red ball bars every entry at ramps, crossovers and one-way mouths, and wrong-way boards mark the forbidden side of one-way streets and split highways, ordering a turnaround short of them. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]
FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A50
No-U-turn boards guard split highways and fast roads, while movement-ban boards veto lane or approach turns from poles or gantries, sometimes echoed by painted arrows. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]
FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A50
One-way boards chain drivers to the arrow’s heading, lane-use boards bless each lane’s allowed move, and keep-right boards steer wheels past islands, medians and mid-road blocks to the shown side. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]
FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A50
No-passing boards map sight-short ground where hills, bends, crossings and driveways hide entering cars, joining paint to open and close passing stretches that may be used only when safe. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]
FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A50
Wheelchair-marked stalls belong to drivers holding disabled privileges alone, and speed boards post the fastest lawful pace for the stretch. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]
FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A51
Caution boards usually wear yellow with black ink in diamond cut, preaching slower wheels and ready brakes, with signal-ahead and lane-shrink variants heralding lights and merging funnels. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]
FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A51
Walker-crossing boards with arrow plaques pin the footpath, flashing beacons guard busy unsignaled crossings, and two-way boards warn the divider is ending. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]
FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A51
School boards slow wheels near grounds and guards, slick-when-wet boards stretch following gaps and soften braking and swerving, and stop-ahead boards preview the octagon. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]
FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A51
Zone-start boards ban passing the cars ahead, merge boards fuse two lanes into one by mutual grace, and small plaques beneath cautions whisper the safe speed for the hazard. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]
FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A52
Split-highway boards order right as roads fork one-way, bend boards flag curves and narrows, and crossing boards with road names preview junctions and forced turns. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]
FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A52
Signs posted before turns and curves use the arrow's shape to show what to expect and may carry a small sign below showing the maximum safe speed, while guide signs—most of which are rectangular—tell where you are, what road you are on, and how to reach destinations [A52].
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]
FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A52
Route shields wear shapes and colors that betray their road rank, interstate, federal, state, city or county, so map-planned trips follow them true. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]
FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A53
Federal route shields repeat the rank-by-shape rule, while brown boards beckon toward parks and playgrounds. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]
FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A53
Blue squares hawk rest, fuel, camps and care, green boards aim at bike paths, lots, mileposts and chosen exits, and mile ticks march each mile from the south and west rims to reckon distances. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]
FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A53
Ever-green info boards print borders, town lines, streams, heights and landmarks of passing interest. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]
FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A53
Orange diamond or square work boards warn of crews, slow detours, crawling machines and shifting pavement, detour boards open the backup path, and flaggers in bright vests with paddles and red flags rule the zone absolutely. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]
FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A53
At rails, never race the train, never strand the car astride the tracks, spare the gearshift mid-crossing, respect the deceptive bulk and pace, and note the blue round-the-clock emergency number posted at every grade crossing. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]
FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A54
A round yellow X with black rail initials heralds the crossing from afar, and the white crossed blades at the rails yield wheels to every train like a yield board. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0054]
FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A54
Where gates and blinkers guard, halt at the first flash before the arm falls, wait out the raised arm and dark lamps, never skirt the lowered arm, and walkers too must heed signals, gates, flaggers and officers. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0054]
FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A54
Portable or fixed message boards broadcast traffic, weather and hazard orders along the road, and every posted direction binds the driver. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0054]
